title: Gorren and the Bumpy Basket
markdown:
Gorren’s tummy gave a wobbly rumble that was not hunger: a wiggly, jiggly worry-rumble, the sort that sits on the biggest smoothest rock and refuses to be a picnic. He sat just outside his cozy cave, ogre hands twisting like roots that had forgotten which way down was. “Oh dear. Where did it go?”

Today was Special Picnic Day, capital letters in the family calendar. The Grobble-Grumps loved Picnic Day the way some people love birthdays and weather. They always used the extra-special basket: bright blue, wobbly wheels that argued with stones, a faint smell of sunshine and blueberry muffins even when it was empty and pretending to be furniture. Today it should have been full of Grizelda Grump’s chewy rock cakes and Halvard Grump’s fizzy moss lemonade, which fizzed as if it had opinions. The basket had simply vanished, which baskets should not.

“Pip! Luna!” Echo in the breezy mountain.

A shimmery spark zipped his ear. Pip the Stone Sprite, pebble-sized, bounced on the nose. “Here, here, here!” Luna Bright the Cloud Weaver settled on a pine, moonlight-soft, voice a quiet breeze. “Hello, Gorren.”

“The basket is gone. We can’t picnic.” Lip wobble, almost a cry.

“A quest!” Pip puffed like a determined marshmallow. Luna: “Perhaps it wandered. Things do.”

“Too heavy. No legs.”

“Then we find it. To the woods.”

Sunspike woods at the foot of the peaks were a little shadowy of an afternoon, not too scary with two best friends and a reason. Pip zoomed, a tiny fast blur of excitement that occasionally circled back to make sure the ogre had not become a statue of worry. Luna floated above, shimmery lantern, secrets in the breeze. They took the winding path. Gorren’s big soft bare feet trod as if the ground were a sleeping guest: no beetles, no delicate wildflowers if he could help it. Wind whistled through rocky ledges and twisted trees, tuneless songs that almost had words. His tummy stayed jelly on a shaky plate. Each step toward the precious blue thing made him a fraction braver, which is how bravery often arrives: not as a speech, as a path.

Pip darted back. “Someone. Odd. Old socks and shiny things.”

Gorren peeked through twisty gnarled mountain bushes, curious and trying not to snap a twig like a confession. There, cross-legged on moss beside a very old crooked oak, sat a goblin: small, wiry, pointy ears twitching, eyes darting like busy fireflies. Flicker, known through the Sunspike Peaks as a collector of everything interesting he could find, a large lumpy sack beside him almost bursting. And there, looking a little embarrassed to be in a goblin scene: the familiar bright blue wobbly-wheeled picnic basket.

Heart flip, then wobble. “That’s my picnic basket.”

Flicker jumped, clutched. “Nonsense. Mine. Sturdy container.” Rusty-hinge squeak.

“Special Picnic Day. Rock cakes. Halvard’s moss lemonade.”

Blink, think-fast. “Had none of that. Empty when I found it. Lumpy inside.”

Gorren frowned. Mother that morning: special rare stones for Uncle Grumbo, the shiny-rock collector. Forgotten in muffin excitement.

Pip buzzed angry-bee. “Took it without asking!”

“Abandoned! New home for my prize collection.”

“Prize?” Gorren peeked the sack.

Flicker produced oddly shaped pebbles, unique, proud. “Most Interesting Bumps. Perfectly bumpy. Remarkably bumpy.”

Not mean: excited, a silly mistake. “You thought empty and lumpy because of the stones.”

Eager nod. “But not quite empty. Your bumpy things.”

Rumble-giggle; oak leaves trembled. “Stones for Uncle Grumbo. He loves them.”

“Rare? Excellent taste. Apologies.” Basket returned. “Would have fitted.”

Lighter in the arms, stones still in the sack’s logic. “You’re a collector like him. That one looks like a tiny sleeping badger.”

Sparkle. “A sleeping badger! Remarkable eye for bumps.”

Luna drifted down. No speech about friendship and misunderstanding. The worry-lake went still. “Share our picnic? Blueberry muffins, now I remember to look.”

Ears nearly to sky. “Delightful.”

They sat on the moss and made a picnic of muffins remembered in time, plus whatever crumbs of pride Flicker would allow about his sack. He told bump-lore: a pebble that looked like a hat, one that sounded almost like a bell if you were kind. Gorren demonstrated the wobbly wheels, which preferred uneven ground the way some people prefer honest weather. They giggled at cloud-shapes and named one Uncle Grumbo’s Eyebrow. Luna whispered almost nothing, which was her best compliment.

Home, basket safe in strong arms, the family cheered as if he had fetched a dragon. Rock cake. Moss lemonade that fizzed like relief and tasted of Halvard’s particular science. Flicker waved from the oak with a pocket of pebbles and a promise of magnificent bumps to make Grumbo’s eyes pop, and a twig already spotted on the path. Gorren bounced upward, adventure finished, picnic properly begun, a new collector on the guest list and the basket’s wheels still arguing pleasantly with stones.
characters: Gorren (Gorren the young ogre), Pip (mountain companions)
